Date: 2026-03-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hybrid storage + model-fallback ops: kickoff

Hi Jasmine —

Great to reconnect. Pinecone is interested in a tightly scoped pilot with Redwood to validate a hybrid storage + model-fallback workflow for customers that need hot vector lookups in Pinecone and S3 cold-tier fallthrough for large corpora. The goal is to demonstrate consistent latency under load while reducing long-tail storage costs.

Proposed pilot scope (2–4 weeks):
- Reference dataset: 10M vectors (producer to provide sample subset)
- Hot tier: Pinecone hosted indexes for <=30 day active set
- Cold fallthrough: S3 object store + pgvector-compatible rehydrate path
- Model-fallback policy: smaller quantized model variant for cold-path reranks, full model for hot-path generation
- Success metrics: 99th-percentile latency under 150ms for hot-path, cost/req reduction >=20% vs all-hot

We attached a short outline (pinecone-hybrid-outline.pdf) with a sketch of traffic patterns and suggested API contracts.

Questions for Redwood to confirm:
- Preferred data-copy/provisioning approach for the sample subset?
- Do you have a preferred mutual action plan template?
- Who should own the ops playbook (runbooks + rollback) on both sides?

If this looks good, Samir and I can schedule a 60-minute kickoff next week and loop in Dev for the architecture deep-dive.

Thanks,
Samir Gupta
Head of Partnerships — Pinecone

Subject: Re: Hybrid storage + model-fallback ops: kickoff — technical notes

Bringing a few technical details to the thread. High level we can support the S3 presigned ingestion flow and a pgvector-compatible cold rehydrate path. A couple of caveats and suggestions:

Technical considerations:
- KV cache warmup: we'll need a short pre-warm window (30–90s) when switching from cold to hot to avoid N+1 penalties; recommend a lambda that triggers on rehydrate to pre-populate popular prefixes.
- Model-fallback policy: implement a lightweight scoring pass (compact quantized reranker, e.g., 4-bit int8 variant) to rank cold results before passing to larger generator. This reduces tokens used on full model runs.
- Kernel selection & batch sizing: we should test per-sequence-length kernels; Dev can provide a small benchmark harness.
- Auth & telemetry: please share a service account for read-only index queries for the pilot; we will instrument traces and token cost breakdowns in the Console.

I attached a quick architecture sketch (hybrid-arch-v1.pdf) that maps traffic flow, rehydrate triggers, and fallback decision points.

Happy to walk through during the kickoff.

- Dev Patel
Sr. Platform Engineer — Redwood Inference
